environment.description: Service deployed behind Kong Gateway (OSS 3.6.x) with a custom request-validator plugin instance configured per-route. The plugin enforces a JSON Schema (draft-2020-12) on the request body for POST /api/v1/settings/merge and POST /api/v1/users/{id}/preferences. The schema uses 'additionalProperties' with a recursive definition that permits only keys matching ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,30}$ at every nesting level via 'patternProperties' and sets 'additionalProperties: false'. Additionally, the schema explicitly lists 'not: {required: ["__proto__"]}' and 'not: {required: ["constructor"]}' and 'not: {required: ["prototype"]}' at each object level using allOf composition. The plugin returns 400 before the request reaches upstream if any property name fails the pattern or if banned keys exist at any depth. Kong is configured with 'untrusted_lua: off' and the plugin is a compiled Go plugin (not Lua) using Kong's PDK, reducing bypass surface. The validator recursively walks nested objects before forwarding.

config.plugin: request-validator (Go PDK compiled plugin, not Lua)
config.schema_enforcement: JSON Schema draft-2020-12 with recursive patternProperties ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,30}$ and additionalProperties:false at all levels
config.banned_key_enforcement: allOf with not:{required:[key]} at every object schema level, recursive
config.rejection_behavior: HTTP 400 with body {"message":"schema violation"} before upstream forwarding
